summary: Establishes the agency's comprehensive risk management program including governance structure, risk identification, and mitigation strategies.
justification: No Corridor row in pages 7–31 governs enterprise-wide risk management as a formal governance program. The Corridor addresses specific risk categories individually — infection control (Section 6, rows 1–16), emergency management (6-037), environmental safety (6-018), and occupational exposure (6-001, 6-028, 6-029) — but has no integrated Enterprise Risk Management program row. ERM as a discipline (governance structure, enterprise risk register, cross-domain mitigation) is a Modern Operational Governance Layer concept that post-dates the legacy regulatory crosswalk scope. Forcing a partial match to any individual Section 6 row would misrepresent the scope of this policy.

summary: Defines requirements for reporting, documenting, and investigating all incidents, near-misses, and adverse events.
realEvidenceArtifacts: Incident report forms with completion date, description, and disposition
Incident investigation log with assigned investigators and resolution timeline
Near-miss event tracking records

justification: Corridor rows 5-005 'Incident Reporting' and 5-006 'Serious Adverse Events' directly govern incident reporting and investigation requirements. RM-ER-002's content — reporting requirements, investigation procedures, near-miss tracking, adverse event documentation — aligns exactly with the combined scope of these two rows. Note: cross-domain semantic overlap with QA-AE-001 ('Adverse Event Identification & Reporting') which maps to the same Corridor rows from a QAPI framing. No contradiction — QA-AE-001 governs QAPI-integrated clinical adverse events; RM-ER-002 governs risk-domain incident management. Different operational triggers, same regulatory grounding. Evidence: P, D, I.

summary: Mandates regular risk assessments across all operational domains with documented risk scoring and prioritization.
justification: No Corridor row in pages 7–31 governs cross-domain operational risk assessment with documented scoring and prioritization methodology. The Corridor addresses domain-specific risk assessments individually: EP plan risk assessment (6-037), infection surveillance (6-014/6-015), environmental safety assessment (6-018). A meta-level risk scoring and prioritization framework that spans all operational domains is a Modern Operational Governance Layer concept — enterprise risk management methodology that exceeds the Corridor's per-category regulatory compliance approach. Forcing a partial match to 6-018 or 6-037 would misrepresent the breadth of this policy.

summary: Establishes requirements for maintaining adequate professional liability, general liability, and workers' compensation insurance.
justification: No Corridor row in pages 7–31 governs professional liability, general liability, or workers' compensation insurance requirements. Insurance management is a business operations and risk finance control that falls outside the Corridor's clinical/regulatory crosswalk scope entirely. ACHC accreditation standards do not address specific insurance requirements in the pages 7–31 crosswalk. This policy belongs exclusively to the Modern Operational Governance Layer.

justification: Corridor row 5-008 'Aggregation of Data/Information' (Section 5) covers data collection and aggregation for performance improvement purposes (HH6-4A, HH7-9A.01). RM-ER-005 applies systematic trend analysis to risk and incident data — a parallel analytical function operating in the risk management domain rather than the QAPI domain. The analytical methodology (aggregate, trend, identify patterns) is structurally consistent with 5-008, but the application is risk governance rather than quality performance improvement, and the cross-domain scope exceeds the QAPI context. PARTIAL with MEDIUM confidence — the structural method matches, but the governance application diverges from the Corridor row's QAPI framing.

No ACHC standard in the Corridor print crosswalk governs litigation response or legal counsel coordination. This policy belongs exclusively to the Modern Operational Governance Layer.

summary: Heat illness prevention for outdoor (8 CCR §3395) and indoor (8 CCR §5141.1, effective January 2025) environments. The Cal/OSHA Heat Illness Prevention Standard (8 CCR §3395 outdoor, §5141.1 indoor effective January 2025) is a California workplace safety regulation that post-dates and falls outside the ACHC Corridor crosswalk's scope. The indoor heat illness standard (§5141.1) is effective January 2025 — newer than the Corridor's general health and safety framework. This policy belongs to the Modern Operational Governance Layer (California-specific regulatory requirement absent from Corridor print scope).
